title.narrative: Hands Off II Mozambique

description.narrative:
Brief overall description: Nearly 70 percent of sex workers in Mozambique report having experienced violence, mainly perpetrated by clients. Aidsfonds, Tiyane Vavasate (sex worker-led group), Pathfinder (international NGO) and the National We Want Rights Platform (national sex worker-movement) work on reducing violence against sex workers in Mozambique. This is done by implementing activities that focus on strengthening the sex worker movement and by building strong relations with allies such as healthcare workers, politicians and law enforcement officers. Human rights violations against sex workers will be documented and used for lobbying and advocacy purposes. With the support of sex worker focal points in the eleven provinces in Mozambique, activities are rolled out on a national scale.
Description of objectives: Hands Off 2 partners work to reduce violence against sex workers at community, national and regional level. In Mozambique, outcomes include a functional and sustainable national sex worker movement and empowering sex workers to influence policies and laws relevant for them. Partners are also working to increased police protection for sex workers, by working closely with the Polícia da República da Moçambique.
Description of target groups: The programme’s primary target group is female, male and transgender sex workers, meaning those who receive money or goods in exchange for sexual services, either regularly or occasionally. In Mozambique, activities also target healthcare workers, policy makers and police officials and officers.
Additional information (if available): The most recent data on sex work shows an HIV prevalence of 28 percent among female sex workers. Around 29 percent of new HIV infections are among sex workers, their clients and men who have sex with men.

comment.narrative: The number is reduced due to some key factors: a)extreme violence in Cabo delgado due to "terrorist" attacks; b)Reduce number of focal points in some districts; c) deficiencies in the provision of the technical support because it happens in a virtual way with the focal points. Thus, the justifications around productivity are always based on the discourse brought by the focal points, and often there is no way to really verify whether the reasons are real or not, if there is no supervision at the local level. Therefore, the approach of involving the platform members in monitoring the activities of the focal points at provincial and district level - since these members are represented there; d) overlapping reporting and activities, since most focal points are also peer educators from other organizations. And they often prioritize the activities of other organizations over the platform. Therefore, we are already starting the process of performance evaluation of the focal points (the volunteer terms end in May 2023), so that based on their performance we can evaluate the continuity or not of the focal points in the platform, and from there recruit new ones that have more availability

comment.narrative: The paralegals under the project will support SW. This data is not up to date yet, will be updated in the next semester, this is also when the newly trained paralegals will report.

There are three reasons for this reduction: (a) despite low literacy among women in this group regarding conflict resolution flows at the local level, they prefer to make agreements with perpetrators of violence since they have the perception that paying for the violence solves the violence problem. Therefore, the focus has been on the immediacy of the solution, negotiating violence for monetary values; b) The procedural delay of some cases due to the needs of procedural investigation (gathering evidence, searching for material proofs, etc) make some women give up on pursuing the cases until they are resolved at the judicial level, associated with the fact that many women in this age group do not publicly assume the activity of sex work. c) The focal points' poor knowledge of the functioning of the justice system weakens their power to support this component, because they do not understand the mechanisms of treatment, the processes, the time, etc. For this reason we started with the training of focal points as paralegals to better follow up cases of violence in the justice system.

title.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing community-led support after violence

description.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing community-led support after violence

comment.narrative: The reduction is justified for the following reasons: (a) the beneficiaries still present low literacy on human rights and because of this they prefer quick solutions in front of a violent situation submitting to negotiation with the perpetrators of violence; c) The work with the community leaders by the Platform at the local level is still not substantial, since it needs a specific approach of intervention. For example, scheduling meetings with the health committees at the local level (where there is a diversity of community leader representation) requires a more structured coordination with the local structures. This means that focal points must be trained in how to work with local structures and how to engage them. d) Weaknesses in the articulation of the focal point with members of the platform member organizations to be able to do joint community mobilization actions with community leaders, and this will be discussed in the bi-monthly platform meeting
